name: Cybersecurity
tagline: Software and services defending against digital threats — a large, established, recession-resilient theme. Unlike most niche areas, several funds are big and liquid, yet after the Oct 2026 re-score none of the curated funds clears the full green-light screen — IHAK, the closest, now has a top-10 just over 50%.
universe_note: A mature theme with 5+ real funds. The split is concentration vs diversification: CIBR/BUG/HACK lean into the big pure-plays (CrowdStrike, Palo Alto, Fortinet, Zscaler); IHAK (4%-capped) and WCBR (equal-weight) spread wider/cheaper. Price, volume, returns and AUM update daily from fund data.
key_tensions: Concentration vs breadth: CIBR/BUG concentrate in a handful of mega-cap cyber names; IHAK caps each stock at 4% (top-10 ~52%) and WCBR equal-weights — very different single-stock risk.
High valuations: cyber software trades at rich multiples; great businesses, but drawdown-prone when growth multiples compress.
Mega-cap overlap: Broadcom/Cisco/Microsoft appear in some funds — you may already own them via tech/Nasdaq funds.
Pure-play vs diversified-tech: HACK/CIBR are cyber-pure; some 'cyber & tech' funds dilute with broader software.
Cost clustering ~0.45-0.60%: not cheap vs broad tech (XLK ~0.09%) — the theme premium must be earned.
benchmark_note: XLK (tech sector, ~0.09%) and IGV (software) are the yardsticks, NOT cyber funds. They show what you pay extra for cyber focus — and how much cyber exposure you already get from broad tech.

memo.thesis: IHAK is the cheapest dedicated way to own global cybersecurity: an index of ~40-48 companies that each earn at least half their revenue from cyber. It's market-cap weighted with a 4% cap per stock at each semi-annual rebalance — so it is less top-heavy than CIBR/BUG, but the ten largest names (Okta, Qualys, CrowdStrike, Netskope, Zscaler, SentinelOne, Palo Alto, Varonis, Tenable, Fortinet) now add up to just over half the fund.
memo.strategy: Passively tracks the NYSE FactSet Global Cyber Security Index: developed + emerging markets, all market caps, companies with 50%+ cyber revenue. Annual reconstitution, semi-annual rebalance, market-cap weights capped at 4% per stock (weights drift above the cap between rebalances).

purity_verdict.text: Genuine cyber pure-play: the index requires 50%+ of revenue from cybersecurity. The top 10 are all dedicated security vendors.

memo.concentration: Top-10 ~51-55% across ~40-48 holdings (Oct 2026); largest ~5-6%. The 4% cap at each rebalance stops any single stock dominating, but the fund now leans on ~10 leaders — past the methodology's 50% red-flag line.
